en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Nineteenth Chapter
Is the term "patti" unconditioned? Yes.
Is Nibbāna a refuge, a shelter, a resort, the ultimate goal, the undecaying, and the deathless?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is attainment unconditioned? Is Nibbāna unconditioned?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there two unconditioned things?
You should not say so …pe…
Are there two unconditioned things?
Yes. Are there two refuges? ... [and so on] ...
Does the intermediate space blow?
One should not say so… [as before] … Is the acquisition of a robe unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*)?
“Yes. “Is nibbāna … [and so on] … the deathless?”
It should not be said so ... [as before] ...
Is the acquisition of a robe unconditioned, and Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes.
"Are there two unconditioned things?
"One should not say so... [and so on] ...
"Are there two unconditioned things?"
“Yes,” he said.
“Are there two refuges …pe… or is there an interval between them?”
It should not be said thus … [and so on] … regarding almsfood … [and so on] … regarding lodgings … [and so on].
Is the acquisition of medicinal requisites as support for the sick unconditioned?
Yes. [And is] Nibbāna …pe…?
Is it not the case that you would not say, "The deathless is the immortal"? ...
[and so on] ... Is the acquisition of medicinal requisites as support for the sick unconditioned? Is Nibbāna unconditioned?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there two unconditioned things?
One should not speak thus …pe…
Are there two unconditioned things?
Yes. Are there two refuges? ... [and so on] ...
“Does the intermediate space blow?
One should not say so … [as before] … “The acquisition of the robe-cloth is unconditioned (asaṅkhata) …” [as before].
Is the attainment of almsfood …pe… of lodging …pe… of medicinal requisites for the sick unconditioned; is Nibbāna unconditioned?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there five unconditioned things?
“One should not speak thus” … [and so on] …
Are there five unconditioned things?
Yes. Are there five refuges? ... [and so on] ... Yes.
“Does the intermediate [space] blow?
“One should not say so…” [and so on].
“The attainment of the first jhāna is unconditioned” (thus all should be expanded in detail). [The same applies to] the second jhāna…
of the third jhāna … of the fourth jhāna … of the base of infinite space …
of the base of infinite consciousness … of the base of nothingness … of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception …
of the path of stream-entry … of the fruit of stream-entry … of the path of once-returning …
of the fruit of once-returning … of the path of non-returning … of the fruit of non-returning …
Is the attainment of the path of arahantship ... the fruit of arahantship unconditioned? Yes.
“Nibbāna … [and so on] … is it the unshakable, the deathless?
One should not say so … [and so on].
Is the attainment of the fruit of arahantship unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned?
Yes. Are there thus two unconditioned things?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … that there are two unconditioned things? Yes.
"Are there two refuges...
[as before] ...or do they blow between them?
"One should certainly not say so... [as before].
The attainment of the path of stream-entry is unconditioned … the attainment of the fruit of stream-entry is unconditioned … [and so on] … the attainment of the path of arhatship is unconditioned.
Is the attainment of the fruit of arahantship unconditioned … is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes.
"Are there nine unconditioned phenomena?
"One should not say so...
[and so on] "...are there nine unconditioned phenomena?"
“Yes.
“Are there nine refuges …pe… that blow between them?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that attainment (patti) is unconditioned (asaṅkhata)?
“Yes. Form is an attainment; feeling is an attainment… [and so on].
Perception...
mental formations...
consciousness?
It should not be stated thus.
Therefore, attainment (*patti*) is unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*).
The Discussion on Attainment is finished.
